Social Communication Questionnaire: 1. Is she/he now able to talk using short phrases or sentences?
Social Communication Questionnaire: 2. Do you have a to-and-fro "conversation" with her/him that involves taking turns or building on what you have said?

Social Communication Questionnaire: 3. Does she/he ever use odd phrases or say the same thing over and over in almost exactly the same way (either phrases that she/he hears other people use or ones that she/he makes up)?

Social Communication Questionnaire: 4. Does she/he ever use socially inappropiate questions or statements? For example, does she/he regularly ask personal questions or make personal comments at awkward times?
Social Communication Questionnaire: 5. Does she/he ever get her/his pronouns mixed up (e.g. saying you or she/he for I)?

Social Communication Questionnaire: 6. Does she/he ever use words that she/he seems to have invented or made up herself/himself; put things in odd, indirect ways; or use metaphorical ways of saying things (e.g. saying hot rain for steam)?
Social Communication Questionnaire: 7. Does she/he ever say the same thing over and over in exactly the same way or insist that you say the same thing over and over again?
Social Communication Questionnaire: 8. Does she/he ever have things that she/he seems to have to do in a very particular way or order or rituals that she/he that you go through?
Social Communication Questionnaire: 9. Does her/his facial expression usually seem appropiate to the particular situation, as for as you can tell?

Social Communication Questionnaire: 10. Does she/he ever use your hand like a tool or as if it were part of her/his own body (e.g. pointing wuith your finger, putting your hand on a doorknob to get you yo open the door)?
Social Communication Questionnaire: 11. Does she/he ever have any interests that preoccupy her/him and might seem odd to other people (e.g. traffic lights, drainpipes, timetables)?

Social Communication Questionnaire: 12. Does she/he ever seem to be more interested in parts of a toy or an object (e.g. spinning the wheels of a car), rather than in using the objects as it was intended?

Social Communication Questionnaire: 13. Does she/he ever have any special interests that are unusual in their intensity but otherwise appropriate for her/his age and peer group (e.g. trains or dinosaurs)?
Social Communication Questionnaire: 14. Does she/he ever seem to be unusually interested in the sight, feel, sound, taste, or smell of things or people?
Social Communication Questionnaire: 15. Does she/he ever have any mannerisms or odd ways of moving her/his hands or fingers, such as flapping or moving her/his fingers in front of her/his eyes?
Social Communication Questionnaire: 16. Does she/he ever have any complicated movements of her/his whole body, such as spinning or repeatedly bouncing up and down?
Social Communication Questionnaire: 17. Does she/he ever injure herself/himself deliberately, such as biting her/his arm or banging her/his head?
Social Communication Questionnaire: 18.Does she/he ever have any objects (other than a soft toy or comfort blanket) that she/he has to carry around?
Social Communication Questionnaire: 19. Does she/he ever have any particular friends or a best friend?
Social Communication Questionnaire: 20. Does she/he ever talk to you just to be friendly (rather than to get something)?
Social Communication Questionnaire: 21. Does she/he ever spontaneously copy you (or other people) or what you are doing (such as vacuuming, gardening, or mending things)?

Social Communication Questionnaire: 22. Does she/he ever spontaneously point at things around her/him just to show you things (not because she/he
wants them)?
Social Communication Questionnaire: 23. Does she/he ever use gestures, other than pointing or pulling your hand, to let you know what she/he wants?
Social Communication Questionnaire: 24. Does she/he nod her/his head to indicate yes?
Social Communication Questionnaire: 25. Does she/he shake her/his head to indicate no?
Social Communication Questionnaire: 26. Does she/he usually look at you directly in the face when doing things with you or talking with you?
Social Communication Questionnaire: 27. Does she/he smile back if someone smiles at her/him?
Social Communication Questionnaire: 28. Does she/he ever show you things that interest her/him to engage your attention?
Social Communication Questionnaire: 29. Does she/he ever offer to share things other than food with you?
Social Communication Questionnaire: 30. Does she/he ever seem to want you to join in her/his enjoyment of something?
Social Communication Questionnaire: 31. Does she/he ever try to comfort you if you are sad or hurt?
Social Communication Questionnaire: 32. If she/he wants something or wants help, does she/he look at you and use gestures with sounds or words to get your attention?
Social Communication Questionnaire: 33. Does she/he show a normal range of facial expressions?
Social Communication Questionnaire: 34. Does she/he ever spontaneously join in and try to copy the actions in social games, such as The Mulberry Bush or London Bridge Is Falling Down?
Social Communication Questionnaire: 35. Does she/he play any pretend or make-believe games?
Social Communication Questionnaire: 36. Does she/he seem interested in other children of approximately the same age whom she/he does not know?
Social Communication Questionnaire: 37. Does she/he respond positively when another child approaches her/him?

Social Communication Questionnaire: 38. If you come into a room and start talking to her/him without calling her/his name, does she/he usually look up

Bush-Francis Catatonia Rating Scale: 1. Immobility/stupor: Extreme hypoactivity, immobile, minimally responsive to stimuli.
Bush-Francis Catatonia Rating Scale: 2. Mutism: Verbally unresponsive or minimally responsive.
Bush-Francis Catatonia Rating Scale: 3. Staring: Fixed gaze, little or no visual scanning of environment, decreased blinking.
Bush-Francis Catatonia Rating Scale: 4. Posturing/catalepsy: Spontaneous maintenance of posture (s), including mundane (e.g. sitting or standing for long periods without reacting).
Bush-Francis Catatonia Rating Scale: 5. Grimacing: Maintenance of odd facial expressions.
Bush-Francis Catatonia Rating Scale: 6. Echopraxia/echolalia: Mimicking of examiner's movements (echopraxia) or speech (echolalia).

Bush-Francis Catatonia Rating Scale: 7. Stereotypy: Repetitive, non-goal-directed motor activity (e.g. finger-play, repeatedly touching, patting or rubbing self); abnormality not inherent in act but in its frequency.

Bush-Francis Catatonia Rating Scale: 8. Mannerisms: Odd, purposeful movements (hopping or walking tiptoe, saluting passers-by or exaggerated caricatures of mundane movements); abnormality inherent in act itself.
Bush-Francis Catatonia Rating Scale: 9. Stereotyped & meaningless repetition of words & phrases (verbigeration): Repetition of phrases or sentences (like a scratched records).
Bush-Francis Catatonia Rating Scale: 10. Rigidity: Maintenance of a rigid position despite efforts to be moved (exclude if cog-wheeling or tremor present)
Bush-Francis Catatonia Rating Scale: 11. Negativism: Apparently motiveless resistance to instructions or attempts to move/examine patients. Contrary behavior, does exact opposite of instruction

Bush-Francis Catatonia Rating Scale: 12. Waxy flexibility: During repositioning of patient, patient offers initial resistance before allowing him/herself to be repositioned, similar to that of a bending candle. (also defined as slow resistance to movement as the patient allows the examiner to place his/her extremities in unusual positions. The limb may remain in the position in which they are placed or not)
Bush-Francis Catatonia Rating Scale: 13. Withdrawal: Refusal to eat, drink and/or make eye contact.
Bush-Francis Catatonia Rating Scale: 14. Excitement: Extreme hyperactivity, constant motor unrest which is apparently non-purposeful. Not to be attributed to akathisia or goal-directed agitation.

Bush-Francis Catatonia Rating Scale: 15. Impulsivity: Patient suddenly engages in inappropriate behavior (e.g. runs down hallway, starts screaming or takes off clothes) without provocation. Afterwards can give no, or only a facile explanation.
Bush-Francis Catatonia Rating Scale: 16. Automatic obedience: Exaggerated cooperation with examiner's request or spontaneous continuation of movement requested.
Bush-Francis Catatonia Rating Scale: 17. Passive Obedience (mitgehen): Patient raises arm in response to light pressure of finger, despite instructions to the contrary.
Bush-Francis Catatonia Rating Scale: 18. Muscle Resistance (gegenhalten): Involuntary resistance to passive movement of a limb to a new position. Resistance increases with the speed of the movement.
Bush-Francis Catatonia Rating Scale: 19. Motorically Stuck (ambitendency): Patient appears stuck in indecisive, hesitant motor movements.
Bush-Francis Catatonia Rating Scale: 20. Grasp reflex: Striking the patient’s open palm with two extended fingers of the examiner’s hand results in automatic closure of patients hand.
Bush-Francis Catatonia Rating Scale: 21. Perseveration: Repeatedly returns to same topic or persists with the same movements.
Bush-Francis Catatonia Rating Scale: 22. Combativeness: Belligerence or aggression, Usually in an undirected manner, without explanation.
Bush-Francis Catatonia Rating Scale: 23. Autonomic abnormality: Abnormality of body temperature (fever), blood pressure, pulse, respiratory rate, inappropriate sweating, flushing.
